title: Level 2 project: a chama contributions tracker
lesson:
Time to build a complete offline app that a real group could use. A **chama** is a savings group: members pay in regularly, and the treasurer has to know who paid what, each member's total, and the group's total. Many treasurers do this in a notebook; a small page on a shared laptop or phone saves arguments and arithmetic.

You'll use every part of this level:
- **A form with validation** (unit 3): member name and amount, errors shown next to each box.
- **State plus render** (unit 4): an array of payments `{ id, member, amount }` is the truth; `render()` draws the payment list, the totals and the grand total from it.
- **Array methods** (unit 5): totals per member with `reduce`, sorted with a compare function.
- **localStorage** (unit 6): saved on every change, loaded on start, safe against broken data.
- **Organisation and accessibility** (unit 8): pure logic separate from the view; labels, a real submit button, an `aria-live` status line.

**Three files, three exercises.**
1. **ex1_chama.html**: the page. A `<main>` with a max-width, the form `#pay-form` (inputs `#member` and `#amount` with labels, HTML checks, error spans `#member-error` and `#amount-error`, and a submit button), a status line `#status` with `aria-live="polite"`, the lists `#payments` and `#totals`, the grand total `#grand`, and the script `ex2_chama.js`.
2. **ex2_chama.js**: the app. Its exercise prompt lists every function and exactly what it must do. The starter lays out the sections (state, logic, storage, actions, view, wiring) so each piece has a home.
3. **ex3_owes.js**: the treasurer's question at every meeting: *who still owes, and how much of the target have we collected?* Pure functions with array methods.

**Plan before you type.** Write the logic first (`validatePayment`, `totalsByMember`, `grandTotal`) and run the tests: they don't need a page. Then storage (`loadPayments`, `savePayments`), then `addPayment`/`removePayment` (change state, save, render), then `render`, and the submit wiring last. Test by hand in the preview too: add payments, remove one, reload the page and check they're still there.

**Think like the treasurer.** What if someone types "  Amina" with spaces? (Trim it.) A blank amount? ("Enter an amount", not 0.) 250.50 shillings? (Whole numbers only.) The browser data was cleared? (Start empty, don't crash.) Someone overpays? (It must not hide another member's debt in the collection percentage.) Every hidden test is one of these real situations.

When it works, it's genuinely useful: the same pattern runs a clinic's stock book, a school's attendance, or a game's save system.

notes: Logic first: nothing changes unless the input is valid.
State is the one array of payments, each with its own id.
Save on every change, so a closed tab loses nothing.
render() draws everything from state, so lists and totals always agree.

exercises.title: The tracker app
exercises.prompt: Write the tracker (the page is ex1_chama.html). State: var payments (an array of { id, member, amount }) loaded with loadPayments() on start, and var nextId continuing after the biggest saved id. validatePayment(member, amount) (both text): errors.member = "Enter a member name" if blank after trimming; errors.amount = "Enter an amount" if blank, or "Amount must be a whole number above 0" if it isn't a whole number above 0; returns {} when fine. totalsByMember(list): an array of { member, total }, biggest total first, ties A to Z. grandTotal(list): all amounts added. loadPayments(): the array saved as JSON under "chama.payments", or [] if missing, broken or not an array; keep only items with a whole-number id, a text member and an amount above 0. savePayments(): saves payments as JSON under that key. addPayment(member, amount): if invalid, return the errors object and change nothing; otherwise add { id: nextId++, member: trimmed, amount: as a number }, save, render, return {}. removePayment(id): remove it, save, render. render(): empty and redraw #payments (one <li> per payment holding a <span> "MEMBER: AMOUNT KSh" and a <button> "Remove" that removes that payment), #totals (one <li> "MEMBER: TOTAL KSh" per totalsByMember row) and #grand ("Total: N KSh"). On submit of #pay-form: preventDefault; addPayment with the two boxes; show each message (or "") in #member-error / #amount-error with the class "invalid" on the box; if it worked, set #status to "Saved AMOUNT KSh from MEMBER" and empty both boxes.

exercises.title: Who still owes?
exercises.prompt: Each member should pay the target amount this month. Write whoOwes(payments, members, target): payments are like [{ id, member, amount }], members is the list of names. Return an array of { member, owes } for each member who has paid less than target (owes = target minus what they paid), most owed first, ties A to Z. Payments from people not in members are ignored. Write percentCollected(payments, members, target): the percentage of (members times target) collected, rounded to 1 decimal, where each member counts at most target (an overpayment doesn't cover someone else); 0 if there are no members or target is 0.

tests.call: whoOwes([{ id: 1, member: "Amina", amount: 500 }, { id: 2, member: "Juma", amount: 300 }, { id: 3, member: "Amina", amount: 700 }, { id: 4, member: "Wanjiru", amount: 1000 }], ["Amina", "Juma", "Wanjiru", "Otieno"], 1000).map((r) => [r.member, r.owes])

hints: First total what each person paid: reduce into an object.
whoOwes: members.map((m) => ({ member: m, owes: target - (paid[m] || 0) })).filter((r) => r.owes > 0).sort(...)
percent: members.reduce((s, m) => s + Math.min(paid[m] || 0, target), 0) / (members.length * target) * 100, then Math.round(x * 10) / 10.

quiz.q: A treasurer reloads the page and all payments vanish. What's missing?
choices: Saving to localStorage on each change and loading on start
quiz.why: Variables only live while the page is open.

quiz.q: Why does every action end with render() instead of updating the totals by hand?
choices: The lists and totals are always drawn from the same state, so they can't disagree
quiz.why: One source of truth, one drawing function.

quiz.q: Why must validatePayment reject an empty amount before converting with Number()?
choices: Number("") is 0, which would quietly record a zero payment

quiz.q: Why does percentCollected cap each member at the target?
choices: So one member's overpayment doesn't hide another member's debt
quiz.why: Each member's share is counted separately.

quiz.q: Which part of the tracker is easiest to test without a browser?
choices: Pure functions like totalsByMember and validatePayment
quiz.why: Pure logic needs only data in and answers out.

cards.a: try { JSON.parse } catch, then Array.isArray, then filter good items.
reduce into an object, Object.entries, map to { member, total }, sort with b.total - a.total.

explain: Explain how your tracker keeps the page, the saved data and the totals in agreement, as if to the group's treasurer.
